note: Richer family + better selection on fm-state (freddiemac_propertystate), 15 seeds.
predicted: Supersedes the DT-* batch, which ran on a mixed code state. Two findings drive this. FIRST, the selection loss dominates: on the first four pools both blend and Ditto leave 47-89% of their OWN ceiling unclaimed, roughly five times the difference between the two families. lambda is chosen from one inner split -- 30% of 70% of a site's rows -- which for a starved site is a handful of events. blend_1se (most conservative lambda within 1 SE, the rule that halved Paper 3's significant losses) and blend_cv (3-fold CV on the target's own training rows) attack that directly. SECOND, our family is poorer than Ditto's: oracle_ditto exceeded oracle_lambda on three of four pools because Ditto re-fits coefficients while blend interpolates two fixed models inside [0,1]. oracle_extrap allows lambda outside [0,1], which is well defined and requires no convex-combination assumption; oracle_rich adds the local intercept refit that section 9 already says is needed under any weight short of zero and that the policy table has never done. oracle_lambda and LAMBDAS are UNCHANGED so section 6's denominators keep their meaning. PREDICTIONS: (1) blend_cv beats blend on mean share across the eleven pools, because averaging the lambda curve over three folds is a strictly less noisy criterion than one split; a 1-seed MIMIC-IV probe gave 31.4% against 27.7%. (2) blend_1se is WORSE than blend on mean -- the same probe gave 12.7% -- because the 1-SE rule pulls toward the local model and most pools here benefit from merging; it should help only on the harmful pools, and that per-pool split is the thing to look at rather than the mean. (3) oracle_extrap exceeds oracle_lambda on every pool by construction, and the question is by HOW MUCH -- if it is under 2 points the extrapolation is cosmetic. (4) oracle_rich exceeds oracle_extrap on the pools with the worst calibration; the probe showed no gain on MIMIC-IV. WITHDRAWAL: if blend_cv does not beat blend, the selection-loss diagnosis is wrong and the gap is oracle optimism rather than a recoverable deficit, which must be said in section 6 instead of a recommendation to change the rule.
